question: In a monostable multivibrator using IC 555, what triggers the output pulse?

options.text: Applying a high voltage of value equal to Vcc at pin 5
Applying a pulse with voltage going below 1/3 Vcc

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Working Principle:**

The IC 555 timer operates as a monostable multivibrator with the following steps:

 
• The circuit starts in a stable state where the output is low (0).
 
• A trigger pulse is applied at the trigger pin (pin 2). This pulse must have a voltage level lower than 1/3 of the supply voltage (Vcc).
 
• When the trigger pulse goes below 1/3 Vcc, the internal flip-flop of the 555 timer is set, causing the output at pin 3 to go high (logic 1).
